notes: The catalogue has arduino-leonardo, so it is used even though the parts list matched it to None. The Leonardo connects to the computer by micro-USB. The USB cable is not drawn, so it is not modelled.
Catalogue convention: bank 't' is rows a-e and bank 'b' is rows f-j. The image's upper half (rows f-j, next to the 5V rail) is therefore bank 'b', and its lower half (rows a-e) is bank 't'.

Each pushbutton straddles the centre gap. Its upper legs (side 1) are in bank b at columns L and L+2, row f. Its lower legs (side 2) are in bank t, row e. L is 6, 11, 16, 21 and 26 for buttons 1 to 5.
Side 1 gets 5V through a red jumper to row h of the right-hand column. Side 2 (the input side) goes to the Arduino pin and to the 10k pulldown resistor, which runs to the GND rail.

Pin mapping follows the schematic: button 1 on pin 6 (mouse click), button 2 on pin 5, button 3 on pin 4, button 4 on pin 3, button 5 on pin 2. The blue wire loops are nested in the image, and the order is the one the schematic shows.
Power rail hole numbers are approximate, read from the image positions. tp is the upper positive rail, which carries 5V. bn is the lower negative rail, which is GND.
The 10k resistors use value=10000. The exact breadboard rows for the blue wire ends (row c for button 1, row b for the others) are read from the image.
